status.label: Installer scope conflict
status.detail: The supplied installer log already identifies an existing all-users PowerToys 0.65 installation blocking the per-user 0.101 installer.

next_action.label: Post corrective install steps
next_action.reason: The reporter can resolve the diagnosed scope guard by uninstalling the machine-wide installation before running a matching installer scope.

judgment.rationale: This is a diagnosed installation-scope guard, not an unknown update bug: the bundle detects PowerToys 0.65.0 as installed for all users and intentionally blocks the per-user package.
evidence: The attached Burn log sets DetectedPowerToysVersion to 0.65.0 and DetectedPowerToysUserVersion to 0.0.0.0.
The installer emits: PowerToys is already installed on this system for all users. We recommend first uninstalling that version before installing this one.
The issue has no comments, assignees, linked fixes, or conflicting reporter follow-up.
judgment.recommended_action: Post the specific uninstall/reinstall guidance; do not request a bug-report ZIP because the supplied installer log is decisive.

issue_context.summary: The per-user 0.101 installer is blocked because an older machine-wide PowerToys 0.65 installation is still registered.
known_information: The reporter pasted the relevant Burn detection log for PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2362.0-x64.exe.
The log detects PowerToys 0.65.0 in the all-users product code and no current-user installation.
The bootstrapper exits during detect with its explicit mixed-scope protection message.
There are no comments, assignees, or linked fixes on the issue.
inferences: The older machine-wide installation may not be obvious from the current user profile, but Windows Installer still reports it as installed for all users.
issue_context.analysis: The existing evidence identifies both the guard and the supported remediation. A maintainer support comment is more useful than asking for unrelated diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Forced 2026-09-02 pass read the complete issue body, labels, empty assignee list, and timeline links; there are no issue comments or linked work.
Matched the error text and detected-version variables to the PowerToys installer mixed-scope guard.
Confirmed the per-user bundle intentionally refuses installation while the per-machine product is registered.

actions.label: Post installer scope guidance

comment.body: The installer log identifies the cause: Windows Installer still detects PowerToys 0.65.0 as an all-users (per-machine) installation, while PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2362.0-x64.exe is the per-user installer. PowerToys intentionally blocks mixing those installation scopes. Please uninstall the existing machine-wide PowerToys entry from Windows Installed apps using an administrator account if required, restart if the uninstall asks for it, and then install 0.101.2362.0 using either the per-user installer or the all-users installer consistently. A bug-report ZIP is not needed for this diagnosed installer guard.
